title: The Relationship between Cognitive and Personal Characteristics Among Students of High-Tech and Humanitarian Education
abstract: The relationship between cognitive and personal aspects of student development as a complex and multifaceted problem is becoming an object of research in the context of studying the psychological factors of university success. Cognitive and personality traits can interact both directly and through mediating factors, influencing learning success, psychological wellbeing, and other aspects of educational and professional activities. Along with this, personal and cognitive characteristics underlie educational and professional choices, thus acting as an important factor in the success of education and professional development at a university. At the same time, it is noted that, both in the cognitive and personal spheres, the question of determining the factors determining the success of learning remains open. The purpose of the study: to identify typo-logical differences in the relationship of non-verbal intelligence with the personal qualities of students, depending on the profile of training (high-tech or humanities). Materials and methods. The sample consisted of 116 high-tech students and 130 university humanities students. Research methods: The Raven Progressive Matrices Test, the Big Five questionnaire (version BFI-2-S), the Intellectual Risk Assessment Scale, the Aspiration Index questionnaire, and the method of diagnostics of subjective well-being. The results of the study. According to the university's study profiles, the factors and types of students are described according to the criteria of severity of non-verbal intelligence and personal qualities (conscientiousness, tolerance to uncertainty, life aspirations and subjective well-being). Both general trends and differences in the characteristics of connections between nonverbal intelligence and significant age-related personal qualities among students of high-tech and humanitarian education are highlighted. Based on the psychological content of the identified factors and types of students, possible psychological predictors of educational and professional success have been identified, which, as a working hypothesis, will be tested taking into account the real results of students’ academic performance at subsequent stages of the longitudinal study.
